campaign: MOSS in overgo does what the MOSS Ultra workflow does in ComfyUI, each section held to ComfyUI's recording

items.title: A training route's dataset, split and processor identities bind the examples and preprocessing it consumes, not the manifest's bytes alone

steps.title: The MOSS route and the codec -frames route bind their training identity to the ordered media they read, so two corpora with one manifest text get two identities
steps.rationale:
SQA-507 (P2), checked by the lead against cmd/train and internal/trainingworkflow at 7e417691c: valid from source, a proof that passes for a dataset it did not read. Both routes pass only the manifest path to openSessionAs; BootstrapRecipe takes TextAuthority of its bytes, so two directories with the same pictures.tsv and different pictures get one dataset, split, processor and recipe, and the validation proof (groundTraining) identifies the MOSS route by the TSV alone. No run with substituted media was observed.

The change: the dataset, split and processor identities bind the ordered examples and the preprocessing the route consumes, through the existing training workflow and artifact identities, so the same inputs keep their identity across directories and different media get another; the session, checkpoint and validation proof use it. First read every reader of the identity BootstrapRecipe gives.

Check: TestTwoCorporaWithOneManifestTextAreTwoDatasets, two directories with one pictures.tsv and red.png's contents differing: two dataset identities; the same media in two directories: one. It calls the route's bootstrap, which the base holds, so it builds there and fails on its assertion.

Note: SQA-514 (P2), answered by the lead on 2026-11-27 at ab55e884d: valid from source. refuseTrainedHeldOut decodes each held-out picture (moss-heldout/do) and admits one whose decoded shape is not [3, size, size], a 16 x 16 picture beside -size 32, so trainMOSS prepares every training picture and caption on the card before the held-out encoder refuses it. At this admission point the change refuses a held-out picture whose decoded shape is not the run's size, naming its path and the size, with the check interleavedRows makes, before any device encoder opens; the route's test of a run refused before its first picture holds a 16 x 16 held-out picture too.

items.title: A tool call whose result says isError fails the call: its mutation is recorded failed and a failed inspection earns no credit, after a restart too

steps.title: decodeMCPResponse reads a tools/call result's isError, and the coordinator records an admitted mutation failed and a failed inspection uncredited
steps.rationale:
SQA-508 (P2), checked by the lead against internal/agenttool/transport.go at 7e417691c: valid from source, a check that passes without checking. decodeMCPResponse returns a result unchanged when the envelope carries no error, so a tools/call result with isError=true, the shape serveTools emits when a worker tool fails, reads as success: closeMutationReceipt writes StageCompleted for the failed mutation, a failed inspection sets session.Inspection, and RestoreSession rebuilds that credit after a restart. No such run was observed.

The change: at tools/call the result's isError is read; the failed tool's text is kept as the call's diagnostic; an admitted mutation is recorded failed and a failed inspection earns no credit, after a restart too; the writer's replies reach the client with the client's request id. Fixtures check the flag true, false and omitted.

Check: TestAToolResultMarkedAnErrorFailsTheCall in both packages, each holding a test of the name; it uses the transport and coordinator the base holds, so it builds there and fails on its assertion.

items.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test

steps.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test
steps.rationale:
The evidence: cuda-synthetic/tag moved every untagged CUDA test that reads the data root behind modeltest but one. TestSenseNovaVariableRequestResources runs SenseNova's 8B production generation in an isolated measurement process, and docs/image_video_capacity.json names its retained measurement by the bytes of its file (evidence:sha256:888854b5...), which the store holds; tagged, its bytes changed and TestImageVideoCapacityAcceptance found no evidence under the new identity. A measurement is taken again only on a card to itself, and the readings campaign holds the card until its Wan arms are drawn, so the file stays in the gate, named by the check as measuredInPlace, and this row follows the campaign.

The change: the test carries //go:build modeltest, it is measured again on a quiet card into the store, the capacity record and its protocol digest (imageVideoCapacitySHA256) name the new identity, and measuredInPlace goes, so internal/sensenovarecipe leaves the cuda lane.

Check: a whole-tree test with measuredInPlace gone, named afresh so it fails before the change: TestTheGateRunsNoRealModelTest.

Refiled 2026-11-16 from cuda-resources/do, whose step carried no card need, so dispatch gave it while the readings campaign held the card: this step carries -needs-card and waits for a card to itself.

items.title: LiveEdit's scorecard row carries a time at the size a person asks for: an edit of a clip at 832 x 480

steps.title: An edit's request at a person's size is its page's own size with a source clip at that size, and LiveEdit's page states its developers' size
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-25, point 3, checked by the lead against the closing run's log: valid. LiveEdit's video-user-size cell (22/105) measured nothing: "the verification of ... LiveEdit states no size of its own, so there is no larger request to measure" (mediacapability.PersonRequest found no default size on its page and a size its runtime does not fill), so its only time is the 32 x 16 request's, 12.0 s in that run. The model runs at 832 x 480, the size it was trained at: the README's sample, 33 frames of the Wan clip at that size, was drawn in 25 s on 2026-11-25.

The change: LiveEdit's page declares its developers' size and frames (read them from its model card and inference code), and an edit's request at a person's size takes its source clip at that size too, the stored Wan clip (file:sha256:aba27ea7...) or one the verification names, so the size timed is a size a person edits at. Then the cell is measured on the card (go run ./cmd/validate -run -model LiveEdit), and the scorecard row carries the time.

Check: TestAnEditAtAPersonsSizeTakesASourceAtThatSize, PersonRequest of LiveEdit's module: the request is lifted to the page's size with a source clip of that size; it calls PersonRequest, which the base holds, so it builds there and fails on its assertion.

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
